R/CR.A/267/1998 JUDGMENT  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

By way of this appeal, the appellant has felt aggrieved as the accused were acquitted by the learned Magistrate for the offence under section 7(1) of the Food Adulteration Act vide judgment and order dated 20.3.1997 in Criminal Case No.9939 of 1986.

2. Before adverting to the facts, it was stated by Mr. Patel that identical matters of the same district were disposed of vide judgment dated 29.12.2008, and therefore, he requested that this matter should also meet the same fate.
However, those matter were disposed of on 29.12.2008.
Mr. R.R.

Marshal learned counsel appearing for the respondents submitted that though the matters were remanded, and in most of the matters acquittal has been recorded by the learned trial court, which fact is not disputed by Mr. Patel.

While remanding the matters, this Court in para-5 has held as under:
"5.

I have perused the record of the case, the judgment referred to above and having heard the learned advocates for the respective parties, I am of the considered opinion that correctness of the report of Public Analyst cannot be ignored without examining the Public Analyst as a witness either by the Court or the accused.

In this view of the matter, it is apparently clear that the trial courts have committed serious error while passing the impugned HC-NIC Page 2 of 5 Created On Wed Mar 30 01:53:26 IST 2016 R/CR.A/267/1998 JUDGMENT orders."
3. However, I have gone through the entire record and proceedings, and therefore, I do not think that this matter requires remand to the trial Court.
Mr. Patel has vehemently relied on the grounds urged in the memo of appeal.

4. The factual scenario as it emerges from the record is that the appellant filed a complaint being criminal Case No. 9939/1986 in the Court of the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Navsari,
against the respondents nos. 1 to 3 under section 7(1) and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

The case of the appellant was that on 6th February, 1986, at about 10.15am, the appellant-complainant visited the business packets of SUMUL pasturized milk from the said shop and after opening the said packets 750 ml of milk was packed in a stainless steel container and Kantibhai Motibhai Limbachiya vs Dineshchandra Chunilal Gandhi & ... on 29 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178767424/
2 thereafter the same was packed and sealed by the appellant in the presence of one Amulukh bhai Lallubhai Naik.

sentences.text:
Thereafter, after following the requisite procedure as prescribed under the provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, and the Rules framed thereunder, the said sample was sent to the Public Analyst Baroda for analysis, which was found to be adulterated and therefore, on the basis of the same, the complaint being Criminal Case No. 9939 of 1986 was filed before the learned Judicial Magistrate HC-NIC Page 3 of 5 Created On Wed Mar 30 01:53:26 IST 2016 R/CR.A/267/1998 JUDGMENT First Class, Navsari.
5.

It is submitted by the learned advocate for the appellant that on the factual scenario learned trial Judge could not have acquitted the accused, who were facing grave charges of committing adulteration.
The grounds urged are that the learned Magistrate ought to have held that the sample itself was adulterated.
Just because the sample was taken in presence of one panch, it was not vitiate the entire trial.

On the factual scenario, it is submitted by Mr. Marshal learned counsel for the respondents that the learned trial Judge has given elaborate reasons and the certificate is given after 8 days which is issued on 21.2.1986.

The learned trial Judge has relied on the decision of the Bombay High Court and going through the principle enunciated by the Apex Court for dealing with the appeals against the acquittal order, and that too, the learned trial Judge has relied on the decision of this Court in the case of Pruthviraj Dahyabhai vs. State of Gujarat, reported in 33(1) GLR 711.
6.
